title: STRUCTURE IS NOT DESTINY
question: Do larger male/female structural edge differences predict larger modeled dynamic consequences, or are structural difference and dynamic causal importance only weakly aligned in the frozen matched-central-brain model?

unit_of_analysis.reason: Collapse repeated input/anchor observations to one edge-level record so edges appearing in many SQ-03B memberships do not dominate the analysis.

secondary: relative_weight_difference = abs(weight_m - weight_f) / (abs(weight_m) + abs(weight_f)) when denominator > 0 else 0

dynamic_outcomes.primary: max integrated_positive_voltage total_effect_magnitude S across all SQ-03D input/anchor observations for the edge

compare: top structural abs-weight-difference edges vs top dynamic-S edges
top structural abs-weight-difference edges vs top dynamic-C edges

weight_magnitude_stratification.purpose: Check whether any structure-dynamics association is merely a consequence of larger absolute synaptic weights.

sq03d1_status_handling.reason: normalized asymmetry ratio A failed the frozen scalar acceptance rule
sq03d1_status_handling.rule: SQ-03E may use C and S because they reproduced across all 32 SQ-03D.1 verification pairs; normalized asymmetry A is not used as an SQ-03E endpoint.

claim_boundary: SQ-03E measures descriptive alignment between structural male/female edge differences and modeled dynamic consequences inside the frozen MoscaQuant matched-central-brain system. It does not establish a biological sex mechanism, population-level statistical significance, organism-level behavior, intelligence differences, or financial utility.
